Early, unsigned build of Silly MIDI Tools: a native macOS app that turns audio into MIDI.

## What's new since 0.2.0

- **New layout.** A library sidebar (Audio and MIDI), a main area and a toggleable inspector replace the single window. The app has a new icon, and an About window that groups every third-party licence.
- **Working folder.** On first launch the Welcome sheet asks where to keep your files. The app creates `Audio/` and `MIDI/` inside it, remembers the folder across launches, and keeps the sidebar in sync with changes made in Finder. You can copy audio into the folder or leave it where it is, and relink a file that moved.
- **Transcriptions save themselves.** A finished (or cancelled, with notes found) run is written to `MIDI/` as a `.mid` file. A file you have edited is never overwritten; a new run lands next to it as `{name} 2.mid`.
- **MIDI editor.** Select, Draw and Erase tools, box selection, snapped move and resize, a velocity lane, Quantize, transpose, nudge, Undo and Redo, per-track mute, solo and hide, and an inspector for typing a note's start, length and velocity. Save with Command-S; switching files, closing or quitting asks about unsaved changes.
- **MIDI import.** Import a Standard MIDI File (type 0 or 1) into your folder byte for byte. Damaged files, type 2 and SMPTE timing are refused and nothing is written.
- **Models download on first use.** Pick a model and the button reads **Download & Transcribe**. Settings now has General and Models tabs, where you can install or delete models.
- **Playback.** Loop, a playhead the roll can follow, bar.beat position and zoom, on both the audio and MIDI screens.
- **Menus and shortcuts.** App menus for the common actions, plus Help, Keyboard Shortcuts (Command-/).
- **Accessibility.** The slice handles work from the keyboard, controls have VoiceOver labels, and appearance can follow the system or be set to light or dark.
- **Fixes found while testing this build:** Export no longer crashes and keeps the `.mid` extension; opening another audio file no longer shows the previous file's notes; "Leave it where it is" works for files chosen in the open panel; a failed model download can be dismissed.

## Models and licences

| Model | Licence | Download |
| --- | --- | --- |
| MuScriptor small, medium, large | CC BY-NC 4.0, non-commercial use only | 0.2 to 2.7 GB, gated on Hugging Face |
| Piano (ONNX) | CC BY 4.0, credit required | 154 MB |
| Basic Pitch | Apache-2.0 | built in |

MuScriptor needs a Hugging Face account, accepted terms and a read token in Settings. The app code is Apache-2.0; third-party licences are in the About window and `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`.

## Known limits

- Apple silicon only, not notarized.
- The editor uses a fixed 120 bpm, 4/4 grid and notes between C1 and B6; saving writes notes, velocities and track instruments only.
- The piano model handles one instrument. No OGG decoding.
- The maintainer's Mac is Intel and cannot run this build, so the arm64 app itself has not been run by hand. Audio playback and VoiceOver were also not checked by hand for this release. Please report anything that looks wrong.
